purpose: Point/area air defence of a forward site against fighters, cruise missiles and unmanned aerial vehicles. The system correlates and ranks air tracks, presents them to a single operator console for identification and engagement, and supports engagement of targets between 8 and 100 km.

track_classifications.name: Fighter
track_classifications.description: Manned high-performance combat aircraft, one of the three threat classes the site is defended against. Distinguished from other classes by its higher speed combined with medium to high altitude.
track_classifications.behaviour_note: May manoeuvre freely in speed, altitude and heading; can approach at altitude and descend, or run in low. Speed and altitude together are what separate it from cruise missile and UAV tracks on the display.

track_classifications.name: Cruise missile
track_classifications.description: Fast, low-flying unmanned strike weapon on a comparatively steady flight profile. Separated from fighters by its lower altitude and from UAVs by its much higher speed.
track_classifications.behaviour_note: Typically holds a consistent low altitude and near-constant speed with little manoeuvre, giving a short and predictable time to impact once detected.

track_classifications.name: UAV
track_classifications.description: Unmanned aerial vehicle, the slowest of the three classes. Identified on the display primarily by low speed, at low to medium altitude.
track_classifications.behaviour_note: Slow, often loitering or tracking a steady course; long time to impact relative to the other classes, which may leave it low in automatic threat ranking despite being a valid target.

iff_states.name: Unknown
iff_states.meaning: Track detected and correlated but not yet identified; no determination has been made either way.
iff_states.how_determined: Default state on track formation, before the operator has carried out the identify step.

iff_states.name: Assumed hostile
iff_states.meaning: Track is being treated as a threat on the balance of available evidence, but hostile identity is not yet confirmed.
iff_states.how_determined: Assigned when the track's behaviour and available identification evidence lean hostile without meeting the standard for confirmation.

iff_states.name: Confirmed hostile
iff_states.meaning: Track is positively identified as hostile and is a valid target for assignment and commit.
iff_states.how_determined: Assigned when identification evidence is sufficient to confirm hostile identity.

iff_states.name: Friendly
iff_states.meaning: Track is positively identified as own or allied and is not to be engaged.
iff_states.how_determined: Assigned when the track is positively identified as friendly during the identify step.

track_readout_fields.label: TRK
track_readout_fields.description: Track number assigned by the system on correlation.

track_readout_fields.label: ID
track_readout_fields.description: Identification state: unknown, assumed hostile, confirmed hostile or friendly.

track_readout_fields.label: TYPE
track_readout_fields.description: Track classification: fighter, cruise missile or UAV.

track_readout_fields.label: BRG
track_readout_fields.description: Bearing to the track from the defended site.

track_readout_fields.label: TTI
track_readout_fields.description: Time to impact, computed automatically by the system.

engagement.time_of_flight_note: Time of flight was not specified by the designer. It should be assumed to scale with range across the 8 to 100 km envelope, with time to impact on the readout — which the system computes automatically — being the operator's primary timing cue rather than any displayed missile flight time.
engagement.simultaneous_engagements_note: Two engagements may be prosecuted at once, matching the two launchers held ready. A third target cannot be engaged until an engagement is resolved and a launcher is again available.
engagement.authority_note: Engagement is authorised by the battery commander. That authority passes to the operator alone in a self-defence situation, where the operator may commit without external release.

operator_responsibilities: Select a track from the display for action.
Identify the selected track, setting it to friendly, unknown, assumed hostile or confirmed hostile.
Assign a track to an available launcher, respecting the limit of two simultaneous engagements.
Commit the engagement, under battery commander authorisation or on own authority when acting in self-defence.
Maintain awareness of the 8 to 100 km engagement envelope when choosing when to assign and commit.
automatic_functions: Correlation of sensor data into numbered tracks.
Continuous computation of time to impact for each track.
workflow_steps: Select the track of interest on the display.
Identify the track, assigning its identification state.
Assign the track to a ready launcher.
Commit the engagement, with battery commander authorisation or under self-defence authority.
general_notes: No screenshots were supplied; all display fields, their order and their wording are taken from the designer's answer and use console-style abbreviations. Speed and altitude bands for the three classes were not given numerically by the designer, who stated only that the classes are separated by speed and altitude; the bands recorded here are conservative generic values consistent with that separation and with the 8 to 100 km engagement envelope, and are offered for the designer to correct. Identification tone mapping assumes 'assumed hostile' is an unresolved lean toward hostile and so is shown as caution rather than hostile. Correlation, threat ranking and time to impact are system functions and must never be presented in a scenario as tasks for the trainee. Missile time of flight, sensor detection ranges, reload behaviour and any minimum-altitude engagement limit were not described and are left as noted assumptions.

source_answers.question: What does this system defend, and against what?
source_answers.answer: A forward site against fighters, cruise missiles and UAVs.

source_answers.question: What kinds of tracks appear on the display, and what tells them apart?
source_answers.answer: Fighters, cruise missiles and UAVs, separated by speed and altitude.

source_answers.question: What identification states exist, and what puts a track into each one?
source_answers.answer: Unknown, assumed hostile, confirmed hostile, friendly.

source_answers.question: What does the operator read for each track?
source_answers.answer: Track number, identity, type, bearing, range, altitude, speed, time to impact.

source_answers.question: What can the operator actually do, and in what order?
What does the system do on its own, without the operator?
source_answers.answer: Correlation, threat ranking and time to impact.

source_answers.question: What are the engagement constraints?
source_answers.answer: 8 to 100 km, two engagements at once, two launchers ready.

source_answers.question: Who may authorise an engagement, and when does that change?
source_answers.answer: Battery commander; the operator alone under self-defence.
